comments.text:
# Delta graft review notes — known mismatches + method (reference for dtx.1/.2/split-sibling cards)

Seed provenance: `saf generate delta -M` (PR #7971 build, §2-fixed re-seed at commit 074325b). Independent read-verification found the matcher's `potentialMismatch` flag has BLIND SPOTS — a graft can be confidently wrong:
- `related` and `fuse-fallback` grafts bypass the semantic check; a high `semanticScore` does NOT prove the body is correct.
- DISA reuses SRG/CCI tags across unrelated requirements, so even `srg-deterministic` grafts can be wrong.

Read-verified WRONG grafts (title vs what the carried body actually tested):
- SV-234845 — SLES "directory GROUP-owned by root"; source tested USER ownership (`! -user root`). [now empty -> split-sibling card: author fresh, check group ownership]
- SV-234975 — SLES audit records for `/run/utmp`; source audited `/etc/sudoers`. [now empty -> split-sibling card]
- SV-255921 — SLES "restrict the kernel message buffer" (kernel.dmesg_restrict); source tested sticky-bit on world-writable dirs. [now empty -> split-sibling card]
- SV-234964 — SLES "auditing package installed"; body is `package('sudo')` (from RHEL SV-258083). [flagged primary -> review card dtx.2: assert the audit package]

Method for the review/authoring cards: read each control's SLES check/fix text and confirm the body evaluates THAT requirement; never trust a graft because it parses or scored high. For dense SRG families (audit, PAM/password, crypto/FIPS) review the whole block, not just flagged members. Per-control match data lives in delta.json links[] (oldId, semanticScore, relationship, potentialMismatch).

Title: Review the 193 delta-grafted SLES 15 controls for semantic correctness

Description:
193 controls carry RHEL9 implementations grafted on by `saf generate delta`. The matcher's flag has known blind spots, so grafts can be confidently wrong. This card reviews each grafted body against its SLES STIG check text and fixes mismatches — prioritizing the 15 `potentialMismatch` primaries, then spot-checking the dense SRG families where the matcher is weakest. Done = every reviewed control validates its actual SLES requirement per the profile-development-rubric. Design refs: profile-development-rubric, /private/tmp/saf-delta-findings.md, delta.json links[] (semanticScore/oldId per control).

Files:
- Modify (15 flagged primaries — review each, fix if wrong): controls/SV-234800.rb, controls/SV-234802.rb, controls/SV-234806.rb, controls/SV-234807.rb, controls/SV-234831.rb, controls/SV-234859.rb, controls/SV-234864.rb, controls/SV-234903.rb, controls/SV-234904.rb, controls/SV-234963.rb, controls/SV-234964.rb, controls/SV-234978.rb, controls/SV-235028.rb, controls/SV-235029.rb, controls/SV-255922.rb
- Modify (any unflagged controls found wrong during the SRG-family spot-check): controls/*.rb
- Modify (inputs as needed): inspec.yml
- Test: live `cinc-auditor exec` of the reviewed controls against a SLES/BCI target

First failing test:
SV-234964 is titled "must have the auditing package installed" but its grafted body is `describe package('sudo')` (carried from RHEL9 SV-258083). Run `cinc-auditor exec . --controls SV-234964 -t <target>` and observe it asserts the wrong package — the first concrete fix.

Acceptance criteria (Definition of Done, per profile-development-rubric):
- [ ] Each of the 15 flagged primaries has a documented verdict in card notes (correct as-is | fixed) with a one-line reason referencing its SLES check text
- [ ] SV-234964 fixed to assert the audit package, not sudo
- [ ] Every grafted control in the dense SRG families (audit, PAM/password, crypto/FIPS) spot-checked: grafted body vs SLES check text; any that test the wrong resource/target/dimension are fixed
- [ ] Fixed controls use proper InSpec resources (not raw command() pipelines), clear evaluator output, and inputs for site-specific values (rubric)
- [ ] `cinc-auditor check .` reports 214 controls, 0 errors
- [ ] `bundle exec rubocop` clean
- [ ] All work via TDD (failing test first — control fails on non-compliant, passes on compliant)
- [ ] No regressions on controls outside the reviewed set
- [ ] Live tested: the 15 flagged + the spot-check fixes executed against a live SLES/BCI target — determinate pass/fail, no runtime/resource errors; cinc-auditor exec summary pasted in card notes

Verification:
RUBOCOP_CACHE_ROOT=/private/tmp/rubocop-cache ~/.rbenv/shims/bundle exec rubocop --no-server --config .rubocop.yml && /usr/local/bin/cinc-auditor check . && cinc-auditor exec . --controls SV-234964 SV-234806 -t docker://<bci-container> --reporter cli

Decision points:
- When a graft tests a related-but-different requirement than the SLES check (the matcher's blind spot), STOP and rewrite from the SLES check text — do not tweak the wrong test into a different wrong test.
- If a flagged primary is actually correct, that is a valid verdict — record the evidence, do not change working code for the sake of it.

Anti-patterns:
- Do NOT optimize for card-close velocity or speed.
- Do NOT close this card with any AC unchecked — no deferrals, no "lower priority" exceptions.
- Do NOT add rubocop:disable to work around warnings — fix the root cause.
- Do NOT accept a graft as correct because it parses or because semanticScore was high — read the SLES check text and confirm.
- Do NOT limit the spot-check to flagged controls only — the saf-delta-findings report documents unflagged wrong grafts (e.g. srg-deterministic ones).

- CI/CD, thresholds, hardened suite.
